question: We need to log into a supplier portal nobody gives us an API for, click through it and pull a table, on a schedule and from a server. Running headless Chrome ourselves keeps breaking. Which service would you use for that, and what else did you look at before picking it?
summary: Test a scheduled table extraction and an expired portal login. The recorded mentions do not show whether an agent can complete these tasks.

items.title: Test the documented integration
items.finding: The scan found a Token Management API but awarded only partial provisioning credit. The docs already describe account tokens and session persistence. Missing entry files and a JavaScript signup form do not establish an unusable browser. Choose persistent state when the schedule outlives a running session.
items.nextStep: Connect to an authorized fixture portal, log in, extract a known table and persist state using the documented option for the chosen browser library. Start a later invocation, reload state and extract updated rows. Expire the portal session and verify that the job stops with an explicit authentication result or follows the supported login flow.
items.validation: Record expected rows, persistence lifetime and expired-login behavior. Standard reconnect is Puppeteer-only; do not claim it works as a Playwright disconnect.

sources.note: Persistent state versus standard reconnect; dashboard API token.
Puppeteer-only reconnect semantics, deadlines and session termination.

items.title: Recheck the two robots.txt paths
items.finding: The scan found /single-sign-on and /invite no longer answering at the paths allowed by robots.txt.
items.nextStep: Check whether these are stale public links or intentional account routes. Update the declarations or redirects if they point to retired pages.
items.validation: Confirm the intended targets and repeat the same path checks. This is navigation maintenance, not proof of a recommendation effect.
